cells.tense: You are keeping something alive right now without closing your hand around it.
cells.ask: Bring one thing you're tending to a small, finished point this week. Let it be done, and say what letting it end taught you.
cells.core:
You give something what it needs and then you leave it alone to become what it is. Water, light, wait. The growth is happening because you stopped deciding in advance what it should turn into, and that non-decision is doing more work than any forcing would.

There's a moment when this reaches completion. The care lands, the thing can stand, and your grip has no more to do. Opening your hand there doesn't read as loss — it reads as the thing finally standing on its own, which is what you were after. Pick one thing this week. Take it to that finish, and mark the moment it's yours to stop holding.
cells.sheetLine: You care for it without holding it still.

cells.tense: You are already living in a version of this that has not arrived yet.
cells.ask: Pick one thing you're tending. For one day, do nothing to it. No adjusting, no checking, no protecting. Notice what happens when your hands are off it.
cells.core:
You're caring for something by bracing for what it might become. Every need gets met before it arrives, every outcome steered a little, and care has thickened into grip. The thing in front of you is getting managed, not grown. What you're protecting it from is mostly a future you invented.

There's another kind of attention that lets the outcome stay open — enough light for the next step, not the whole road. Sitting in that takes nerve. Pick one thing and take your hands off it for a day. Not forever. Just long enough to see what it does when you stop deciding for it.

cells.tense: The watering has stopped, and the quiet around it is being called self-sufficiency.
cells.ask: Name one thing you'd like to see grow — a skill, a project, a friendship. Tell one person you want it, then take one small step this week.
cells.core:
A thing gets your attention, you check on it because you want to, and it stands on its own without you rearranging your day around it. That's the shape of it when it's working. The care and the rest of your life share a room and neither one goes quiet.

What's in front of you is a version of that with the reach pulled out of it. Something you wanted to grow is sitting there unwatched. You know how to want something. Aim it somewhere. Name one thing you'd like to see grow, say it out loud to someone, and take one small step this week. Not a leap. One step, so the reach has somewhere to land.
cells.sheetLine: You stopped tending, and you called it independence.

cells.tense: People are leaning on you in ways you did not actually agree to.
cells.ask: Notice one thing you do for someone this week that you didn't choose. Say out loud, 'This is because I want to.' Then mean it, or stop.
cells.core:
You've become the one who holds things for other people, and it runs on its own. A need here, a small crisis there, and now what's fragile gets brought to you and you carry it. They'd call you the caretaker. You'd call yourself depleted. Both are accurate about the same arrangement.

That kind of care keeps going without you at the wheel, which is what drains it. Some of it can be handed back. One thing you're carrying that you didn't pick up on purpose — set it down. Not because you don't care, but because caring on purpose is the point. Say what you're doing and why, then mean it or stop.
cells.sheetLine: You're the caretaker nobody asked you to be.
